title: iD Fresh Food to Double UAE Capacity With New Sharjah Factory as It Targets $1 Billion IPO
excerpt: Founder P.C. Musthafa says the Bengaluru-based fresh food company will open its second Gulf production facility by December and list on an Indian exchange by October 2027.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • iD Fresh Food will open a second UAE factory in Sharjah by December 2026, doubling regional production capacity.
  • Founder P.C. Musthafa confirmed plans for a $1 billion IPO on an Indian exchange targeted for October 2027.
  • The company reported revenue of around ₹680 crore ($78 million) in FY2025 with a 20% five-year CAGR.
  • New markets including Singapore, the UK, and parts of the US are planned for entry this financial year.

From ₹50,000 to a Billion-Dollar Listing

iD Fresh Food, the Bengaluru-headquartered company that turned packaged idli batter into a national brand, is preparing for the biggest chapter of its 21-year journey. Founder P.C. Musthafa told Gulf News in an exclusive interview that the company is targeting a "$1 billion IPO" on an Indian stock exchange by October 2027.

"We are not looking at any revenue fundraising, but we have a lot of shareholders who might be looking at some secondary exit," Musthafa said. "Plus, it was more like a childhood dream."

The company has come a long way from its origins: founded in 2005 with ₹50,000 (roughly $600 at today's rates) and a single grinder, iD Fresh now operates in more than 100 cities across 10 countries and employs around 2,700 people. According to India CEO Rajat Diwakar, the company posted revenue of approximately ₹680 crore (about $78 million) in FY2025, growing at a compound annual rate of around 20 percent over five years.

"Growth at any cost is the philosophy of a cancer cell. I didn't want to be a cancer cell."

— P.C. Musthafa, Founder, iD Fresh Food

Doubling Down on the Gulf

The IPO plan runs in parallel with a major UAE expansion. iD Fresh will open a new factory in Sharjah by December, nearly a decade after establishing its first regional production facility in Ajman. The new plant will double the company's Gulf production capacity.

"We got this factory around 10 years back," Musthafa said from the Ajman site. "At that time, we thought the market was this size. Now the market is already much bigger. We have to look at what the market will be in the next 10 years."

The Ajman facility currently runs three production lines — batter, parathas and chapatis — following the same no-preservatives philosophy that defines the brand. Every raw material is tested before entering the factory, and finished products pass through a check-weigher and metal detector.

A Clean-Label Bet

Musthafa's approach to food manufacturing is uncompromising. The company uses no preservatives, artificial flavours, coating agents or stabilisers. Its batter follows a traditional process: soaking, stone grinding, natural fermentation.

"I will not add any ingredients in the food that my mother cannot identify," he said. "The product is exactly the same thing that my grandmother used to make. We do it at a larger scale."

This discipline extends to waste management. iD Fresh once lost 90 percent of unsold product. The company now uses AI-powered demand forecasting at the store and route level, bringing batter wastage below one percent — for a product with a seven-to-eight-day shelf life.

New Markets and New Products

iD Fresh is preparing to enter Singapore, the UK and parts of the US with its fresh product range this financial year, adding to markets where its frozen parathas and coffee decoctions are already sold. Regional taste preferences are shaping the pipeline: research found that 62 percent of paratha customers in Saudi Arabia prefer peri-peri flavours, so a Peri Peri Parotta and a Zaatar Paratha are both due within two months.

On the nutrition front, a protein-enriched batter made with ragi delivers 15 grams of protein in two idlis — more than two eggs. A second version designed for dosas, targeting roughly 40 grams of protein per serving, is launching within two months.

What It Means for the Diaspora

For Indians abroad who have long struggled to find fresh, preservative-free staples from home, iD Fresh's expansion is personal. The company's UK and US entry plans would bring stone-ground batter and fresh parathas to markets currently served mainly by frozen alternatives. Musthafa frames the UAE as his growth anchor: "UAE is my Sehwag. Every time there's a target, we make it up from the UAE market."
